conventions.convention: Recentering is θ_x μ(B)=μ(B+x), so an occurrence at x moves to zero.
Intensity is Eη(Q) for Q=[0,1)^d; spatial ergodicity concerns the full real translation action, with event invariance modulo null sets separately for every translation.
Factorial pairs exclude equal occurrence indices, rather than equal locations; the reduced measure uses anchors in Q and displacements X_j−X_i, without division by intensity.
The full Palm law retains the distinguished origin occurrence and is characterized by the refined Campbell identity.
Pair correlation satisfies α_red^(2)(D)=ρ²∫_D g; K uses closed balls and deletes exactly one origin occurrence, with K(r)=ρ⁻²α_red^(2)(B[0,r]).

The border procedure retains anchors whose entire closed radius-r ball lies in W, counts ordered occurrence pairs, divides by estimated intensity times eligible-anchor count, and returns not defined when that count is zero.
The stationary-sequence mean theorem starts at index 1, assumes strict stationarity and integrability, and uses no choice axiom.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice as carried by the point-process supplier. For every stationary locally finite point process η on R^d with finite positive intensity ρ, there is a unique probability law P⁰ on the configuration space satisfying E∫h(x,θ_xη)η(dx)=ρ∫∫h(x,μ)P⁰(dμ)dx for every nonnegative product-measurable h. Moreover, P⁰-almost every configuration has at least one occurrence at the origin.
Assume AC and Countable Choice. A stationary locally finite point process with 0<ρ=Eη([0,1)^d)<∞ has mean measure ν(B)=ρλ_d(B) for every Borel B.

Under the stated AC and Countable Choice conventions, for a stationary locally square-integrable point process with 0<ρ<∞, α_red^(2)(D)=ρ∫(μ−δ_0)(D)P⁰(dμ) for every Borel D; subtraction removes one occurrence.
The map (x,μ)↦θ_xμ from R^d times the evaluation-measurable space of locally finite counting measures to that space is measurable.

A real-valued strictly stationary sequence (X_n) indexed by n≥1 with E|X_1|<∞ has an integrable L1 limit of its Cesaro averages. No independence or ergodicity is assumed, and the proof uses no choice axiom.

Assume the stated AC and Countable Choice conventions. For a Poisson point process with locally finite sigma-finite intensity ν, E∫h(x,η−δ_x)η(dx)=∫E[h(x,η)]ν(dx) for every nonnegative product-measurable h, equivalently E∫f(x,η)η(dx)=∫E[f(x,η+δ_x)]ν(dx).

concerns.concern: The Statement writes E[η(Q) | I_η], while def-stationary-point-process-and-intensity defines I_η on configuration space, and η may originally be defined on another probability space. Proof 1.1 correctly moves to the canonical configuration space. Explicitly state that the displayed conditional expectation is computed canonically and composed with η, or use the pullback sigma-algebra on the original space.
